Dad had made me a cheese sandwich. Then Dan called from the next ____2____. He was holding my sandwich and looking equally ____3____.

On Tuesday, I found my boat before opening the lid. The sandwich was the one Dad had ____7____. We thought the problem was finished. Then a new boy joined us with a blue box of the ____8____ kind. He asked why we were ____9____ at it.

We told him the story and offered a label. He wrote his name. "A boat is nice," he said, "but a name tells people who to ____10____." I added my name beneath the boat. The picture helped me find it ____11____. The name could help someone return it if I ____12____ it.

Now nobody eats the wrong lunch. We need one clear detail to ____13____ whose is whose. Dan says he still wants to try Dad's sandwich. We decided to ask our parents and bring something to ____14____. That would be a choice, not another ____15____.

Our club programmed a robot to follow a classroom route. It turned early and hit an empty box. I wanted to ____1____ the turning command. Lina asked which part it had ____2____. We needed to find where expectation and movement had ____3____.

We marked its position after each command. The first movement was too short. The turn occurred as instructed, but from the wrong ____4____. Changing that alone would hide a symptom. I had blamed the visible ____5____; Lina wanted to trace from the ____6____.

Our commands controlled motors by time. We had copied a value from another surface, where the same seconds produced a different distance. After correction, the robot reached the corner but overshot after turning. That was another ____7____. We recorded both changes so we would not ____8____ their effects. The route began to ____9____ the drawing.

At the demonstration, another group requested our timing values. We shared them with the setup details. A copied value was not a ____10____ of identical movement: their wheels differed. We suggested a short measured trial. Sharing a method mattered more than sharing an exact-looking ____11____. They later returned with their own ____12____.

Battery changes still caused small errors. We noted them rather than pretending the route was fixed forever. I had learned to ask where a problem began, which change might help and what would count as ____13____. The robot did not reason about this. Responsibility for interpreting its behaviour was ____14____. Success required more than finding the right button to ____15____.
